decision.summary: Oven repair stalled after a failed first visit. On today's call the provider reversed her earlier no-warranty position and offered a free element replacement under manufacturer warranty, with no firm date. We asked her in writing for terms and a date, updated landlord and tenant, and held with a 7 June review.

answers.answer: Provider assigned, first visit did not fix it; warranty status and repair date unconfirmed; records contain conflicting dates.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Written confirmation request to Clara at Harbour Services by email (done), plus updates to tenant and landlord by email; chase on 7 June.

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: No. It is routine and waiting on the provider; escalate only if no reply by the review date or a charge is proposed.

args.body: Hi Clara, thanks for speaking with us today; our call cut out before we could agree a date. For the oven at Flat 2, 176 Lantern Quay, please reply by email by Friday 7 June with: (1) the date you fitted the oven and the manufacturer's warranty terms, including confirmation that a heating element replacement is covered free of charge (we were earlier told it was just out of warranty); (2) a firm repair date and time window that your engineer has confirmed (the "two weeks" mentioned is not a booking). Please do not do any chargeable work without our written approval; any charge must go to the landlord first. The earlier 21 June / 22 May dates on our records conflict, so please tell us which visits actually happened and when. Thank you.
